dedupe_keys.name: fire evacuation simulation of a humanitarian settlement in the kutupalong refugee camp cox s bazar bangladesh

description: This case study tests a method for assessing fire evacuation safety in humanitarian settlements, using the Pathfinder pedestrian simulation model on a community within the Kutupalong refugee camp in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. It is published in Fire Technology (July 2023) by Erica Kuligowski, Steve Gwynne, Hui Xie, Aaron Westbury, Danielle Antonellis and Christine Pongratz, with affiliations including RMIT University, Lund University and Jensen Hughes. Settlements of displaced people are prone to fire as a secondary incident because of flammable building materials and unsafe fire and electricity practices. The study examines four factors: occupant density, pre-travel delay, route choice and restricted routes. Pathfinder, widely used for building evacuation, coped with the settlement scale, and evacuation times were sensitive to all four factors, with long times that could be serious in fast-moving fires. Coverage: one community in Kutupalong camp. Access: open-access article. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: results depend on the data and assumptions used to configure the model; the model files are not released. Simulation uses: evacuation planning and fire safety in camps and informal settlements. Related records: JuPedSim and the Pathfinder evacuation drill dataset.
name: Fire evacuation simulation of a humanitarian settlement in the Kutupalong refugee camp, Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh
outcomes: Pathfinder could represent community evacuation from a settlement fire; evacuation times were sensitive to density, pre-travel delay, route choice and blocked routes, and the longer times could have serious consequences in fast-moving fires.
resources_used: Settlement layout of a community in Kutupalong camp
